content: We need to determine number of carbonyl (C=O) groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of the molecule. We can use IR spectra to detect carbonyl stretch, or carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-210 ppm). Probably easiest: get IR spectra and look for strong C=O stretch around 1700 cm-1. Use ir_spectra tool. Then count peaks? Might be ambiguous. Could also get carbon NMR and count signals in carbonyl region. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool. That returns a string with peaks and chemical shifts. Then count number of peaks in ~190-210 ppm region. That gives number of carbonyl carbons. Likely each carbonyl gives one carbon signal. So do carbon_nmr_spectra.
